# SB-1024 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P2, line P2-L2
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Hazard description
Airborne dust generated by blasting operations in the Ring Rolling area can present inhalation, slip, electrical contamination, and equipment fouling hazards. Dust from media attrition, degraded coatings, and removed surface contaminants can remain suspended in work zones and re-deposit on nearby controls, motors, and heat-exchange surfaces. In addition to immediate respiratory irritation for personnel, accumulated dust can mask visual indicators, obstruct ventilation intakes, and compromise electrical connectors. The potential for secondary ignition is elevated where dust coats hot surfaces or electrical enclosures. This bulletin focuses on controls and administrative measures to reduce exposure and prevent equipment degradation related to blasting activities adjacent to the Ring Rolling induction billet heater identified as EQ-P2-L2-IH01.

Background and rationale
Recent observations during blasting adjacent to line P2-L2 documented visible dust migration into the Ring Rolling enclosure and onto sensitive equipment surfaces. The presence of conductive or hygroscopic residues on electrical components increases the risk of nuisance trips and corrosion. Housekeeping alone will not fully mitigate airborne transport during blasting; a combination of engineering containment, targeted PPE, modified work sequencing, and documented lubrication and maintenance practices is required. Controls recommended here align with established process and safety expectations in QS-PROC-07 and with local operating procedures SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-05.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P2-L2-IH01 (Ring Rolling induction billet heater). Note: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938.
- Motors, drives, sensors, and control panels located within the P2-L2 enclosure or within the documented blast drift path.
- Fixed ventilation intakes and filtration elements serving the P2-L2 line.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Temporary physical containment: install flexible containment barriers and closing flaps at the blast interface to limit direct dispersion into the Ring Rolling enclosure. Ensure barriers do not obstruct emergency egress or access to safety devices.
- Directed local exhaust: position portable capture hoods with inline filtration between the blast area and sensitive equipment when blasting cannot be isolated by distance or complete barriers. Route exhausted air to safe discharge points using continuous ducting to prevent re-entrainment.
- Seal penetrations: apply removable gasketing or tape over open cable penetrations and panel seams on equipment adjacent to the blast zone prior to blasting. Remove and inspect seals after cleaning before restoring service.

Administrative controls
- Work sequencing: schedule blasting operations during times of minimal Line P2-L2 operation or during designated maintenance windows to limit personnel presence and exposure.
- Pre-blast checks: consult SOP-P2-L2-01 for isolation checklists and confirm that sensitive equipment has been de-energized or protected according to SOP-P2-L2-05 when applicable.
- Area notification: issue advance notice to affected trades and control room personnel with clear boundaries for the temporary exclusion zone.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Require fit-appropriate respiratory protection for personnel performing or supervising blasting where engineering containment or exhaust does not fully control airborne dust. Selection and fit-testing must follow site respiratory program and QS-PROC-07.
- Require eye protection and protective clothing to limit skin contact with abrasive residues.

Operational and maintenance measures
- Post-blast cleaning: use HEPA-filtered vacuums for deposition removal on and around EQ-P2-L2-IH01, control panels, and ventilation intakes. Avoid dry sweeping that re-entrains dust.
- Inspection and lubrication: after cleaning, inspect electrical connectors and motor cooling passages. Apply lubrication and protective corrosion control as directed by maintenance procedures. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938; document its application on the maintenance log entry for the asset.
- Filtration checks: inspect and replace intake and portable filter cartridges per serviceability guidelines recorded in maintenance logs and as referenced by SOP-P2-L2-05. Capture filter disposal records in waste management logs.

Examples and practical scenarios
- Example A: When blasting must occur within the same room as EQ-P2-L2-IH01, set up dual containment: a temporary curtain at the blast boundary and a portable local exhaust hood positioned between the blast face and the heater intake. Evacuate nonessential personnel from the enclosure and record the operation in the local shift log.
- Example B: For short, intermittent grit removal where full containment is impractical, apply panel sealing on adjacent equipment, operate continuous HEPA vacuuming, and limit blasting duration. After completion, perform a targeted visual and vacuum cleaning of EQ-P2-L2-IH01, then note CFW-LUB-938 application in the equipment maintenance record if lubrication is disturbed during cleaning.

Records to keep
- Pre-blast notification log: time, personnel notified, containment methods employed, reference to SOP-P2-L2-01 or SOP-P2-L2-05 as applicable.
- Cleaning and inspection log: description of cleaning method, areas cleaned, photographic record where possible, and confirmation that HEPA vacuums were used.
- Maintenance log for EQ-P2-L2-IH01: record any application of CFW-LUB-938, who performed the work, and any observations of deposits, corrosion, or component fouling.
- Filter and waste disposal records: identity of filters removed, containment of used media, and disposition documented per waste handling procedures.
- Incident and deviation reports: any excursions, personnel exposure incidents, equipment faults, or unexpected ignitions recorded and routed according to QS-PROC-07.

Implementation and follow-up
- Supervisors for P2-L2 shall brief affected crews on these controls prior to the next blasting event and update the shift handover records. Compliance will be reviewed during the next scheduled safety audit and during ad hoc inspections following any blasting activity that occurs without full containment.
- Reference material: review QS-PROC-07 for process safety expectations and SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-05 for local operating and maintenance procedures when preparing for and performing blasting adjacent to the Ring Rolling system.

Effective date
Effective immediately.
